source.title: Learning Associative Memories with Gradient Descent
source.authors: Vivien Cabannes; Berfin Şimşek; A. Bietti

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own gradient-training results for a simplified associative-memory model, including successful classification when capacity suffices and forgetting/suboptimal classification in limited-capacity cases. These results refine the broad training claim but do not test the named CIFAR, initialization, normalization, or deep-network recipes.
record.gate_note: The study tests a different, fixed-embedding linear associative-memory model with cross-entropy. It reports explicit classification outcomes and margin behavior for that model and for a small Transformer task. The paper's discussion of cited work on edge-of-stability and normalization is not its own result. No CIFAR benchmarks, random-label memorization tests, initialization comparisons, or normalization ablations are reported.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes cross-entropy training of fixed-embedding linear associative memories and a simplified Transformer. Loss spikes, eventual convergence and sharpness trajectories are related to V5, but it does not establish recovery above an initial linearized stability limit or threshold-tracking sharpness in the systems V5 describes. None of its results tests V1–V6 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors attribute transient oscillations and benign loss spikes to embedding correlations and frequency imbalance, show eventual perfect classification in their separable overparameterized setting, and illustrate suboptimal cross-entropy memorization under limited capacity. Small Transformer experiments exhibit related qualitative behavior.
record.recipe_differences: Fixed-embedding linear associative-memory model trained with cross-entropy, plus small Transformer experiments; differs from the original wide-network squared-loss stability-limit recipe. The paper studies full-batch gradient descent and does not establish recovery above an initial linearized stability limit.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate, input-embedding correlation, token-frequency imbalance, embedding dimension/capacity, and whether one or three Transformer matrices are trained affect oscillations, loss spikes, and convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Correlated embeddings and frequency imbalance produce transient loss spikes and margin oscillations; larger learning rates accelerate eventual convergence in separable associative memories. Related behavior appears in simplified Transformers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-entropy associative-memory training can recover from interference-driven loss spikes while benefiting from larger learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports excess classification risk of 0.27 and 0.22 for N = 3 and N = 30, respectively, with d = M = 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In capacity-limited associative memories, minimizing cross-entropy can produce worse classification than the best attainable classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5 shows sharpness tending toward zero in the separable regime and describes persistent oscillations around a nonseparable loss minimizer when η > 2/H*.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Associative-memory sharpness dynamics depend on separability; large-step oscillations need not imply neural-network edge-of-stability tracking.

record.problems: The experiments use simplified fixed-embedding associative-memory models and a small Transformer task, not CIFAR convolutional benchmarks. Several outcomes are presented only in plots without numerical values in the supplied text. No controls or uncertainty estimates are reported for these experiments. The discussion notes omitted factors in larger models, including normalization layers, adaptive optimizers, noisy data, and interactions between layers.

untested.parts: All: convolutional-network training error on CIFAR, label corruption, and size, stopping and regularization comparisons.
All: ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and additional student neurons.
All: depth degradation, residual shortcuts and special initialization recipes.
All: activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonality comparisons and trainable depth.
All stated mechanisms: recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, divergence boundaries, and full-batch neural-network sharpness tracking or divergence below the initial threshold.
All: batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The original V5 limits_scope verdict is unsupported: a different setting without the claimed threshold measurements does not establish a scope limitation. Figure 5 is an omitted related result, but does not warrant a version-linked missing entry. States marked cannot_determine indicate inability to assess a listed version, not absence of the study's reported phenomena.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, convolutional networks, SGD or Adam from random initialization, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima frequency, and excess student width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth effects, and the cited special-initialization or Fixup comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth comparisons.

The paper varies learning rate in associative-memory settings and reports loss spikes and accuracy changes, but does not test recovery above a linearized-model stability limit, edge-of-stability sharpness dynamics, or the cited full-batch neural-network results.
Batch-normalization comparisons, accuracy-speed comparisons across normalization settings, and Fixup versus normalization.

rows.subject: associative memory model (N = d = 2)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from null initialization with learning rates η = 10 and η = 1 on the two-particle correlated, imbalanced setting; trajectories and losses shown.
rows.measure: Training loss and 0-1 accuracy over training
rows.value: Figure 2 plots both learning-rate trajectories; the text says large learning rates can cause spikes of both loss and accuracy.
rows.note: Figure values are not numerically transcribed in the supplied text. The text describes loss and accuracy spikes for large learning rates.
rows.check: Loss spikes at η = 1 and 10 do not establish where either rate lies relative to a stability threshold. Figure 2 reports L01, a classification error, rather than accuracy.

rows.subject: associative memory model (N = 2)
rows.operation_detail: One gradient-descent update from W0 = 0 with learning rate η; a lower bound on training loss is derived for αp1 − p2 > 0.
rows.value: L(W1) ≥ η(αp1 − p2)p2, which can be arbitrarily large
rows.note: The result establishes potentially large loss after the first step; it does not establish stability-limit recovery or divergence thresholds.
rows.check: The one-step loss bound is a valid theoretical result, but establishes neither recovery nor a stability threshold. It cannot measure V5's effect.

rows.subject: associative memory model (N = 5, M = 5)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with different dimensions and learning rates on random embeddings; training margins are plotted.

conditions.value: η = 3, 20, and other values shown in Figure 6
sampled uniformly at random on the sphere

rows.measure: Margins for training associations; positive margins indicate perfect accuracy
rows.value: Figure 6 shows faster increase with larger step-size, with more oscillation; when d < N the model lacks capacity to learn all associations and favors frequent ones.
rows.note: The text describes the plotted trend but precise per-margin values are figure-only. The d < N cases expose a capacity limitation.
rows.check: Margin growth and capacity limitations in this linear associative memory do not test V5. Figure 6 uses η = 3 and 10 for d = 3, and η = 3 and 20 for d = 5 and 10.

rows.subject: simplified two-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent training only WO2 in the induction-task setup.
rows.measure: Training loss and margins for five tokens
rows.value: Figure 7 shows loss and margin trajectories; text says margins tend to increase and large learning rates speed loss optimization at the cost of some spikes and margin oscillations.
rows.note: The training setup and qualitative outcomes are stated, while individual plotted values are not.
rows.check: Faster optimization with spikes does not establish recovery above a stability limit. The WO2-only loss panel lists η = 20, 50, 100 and 200; the record incorrectly assigns the jointly trained panels' η = 2, 5, 10 and 20.

rows.subject: simplified two-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent training WO2, WK1, and WK2 together in the induction-task setup.
rows.measure: Training loss and margins for five tokens
rows.value: Text reports more frequent loss spikes at large learning rates, but small final losses, increasing margins, and faster convergence at larger embedding dimensions.
rows.note: Authors say small final losses suggest the induction-head mechanism is learned; no exact final values are stated in prose.
rows.check: Small final losses following spikes are reported, but rates are not located relative to an initial stability limit and sharpness-threshold tracking is not measured.

rows.subject: associative memory model (d = M = 2, N = 3)
rows.operation_detail: The paper analyzes the 0-1 loss of a cross-entropy minimizer in the limited-capacity regime.
rows.measure: Excess 0-1 risk of a cross-entropy minimizer relative to the best possible 0-1 classifier
rows.value: Figure 4 labels excess risk E = L01(arg minW L(W)) − minW L01(W); text states the minimizer can forget the most frequent association.
rows.note: This is a reported limitation of cross-entropy minimization in the toy model; exact plotted excess-risk values are not reliably assignable from the supplied flattened text.
rows.check: Surrogate-loss miscalibration in a capacity-limited linear classifier fits no version. Figure 4 explicitly gives excess 0-1 risk E = 0.27 for N = 3; the record overlooks this readable value.

rows.subject: associative memory model (d = M = 2, N = 30)
rows.operation_detail: SGD trajectory in the limited-capacity setting; the text describes competition and convergence to a suboptimal loss minimizer.
rows.value: Text says competition can erase most memories and that the cross-entropy minimizer can forget the most frequent association; Figure 4 shows a suboptimal minimizer.
rows.note: The available text supports the qualitative outcome; precise plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Suboptimal classification under capacity limitations fits no version. Figure 4 explicitly gives E = 0.22 for N = 30. Its trajectory plots L01, rather than accuracy; the specific most-frequent-association example is stated for N = 3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Associative-memory model with correlated embeddings or insufficient capacity; tested learning-rate trajectories
reader_labels.reason: Large rates can produce loss and accuracy spikes, and limited capacity can prevent all associations from being learned; the study does not test the stated stability-limit recovery mechanism (R1–R5).
